(a) In General.—Section 1601(d) of Public Law 96–607 (94 Stat. 3547; 16 U.S.C. 41011(d)) is amended—

        (1) in the first sentence—

            (A) by inserting a period after “park”; and 
            (B) by striking the remainder of the sentence; and  
        (2) by striking the last sentence.  
    (b) Technical Correction.—Section 1601(c)(8) of Public Law 96–607 (94 Stat. 3547; 16 U.S.C. 41011(c)(8)) is amended by striking “Williams” and inserting “Main”.

fable.w: The section only makes textual edits to Public Law 96-607: inserting a period, striking the remainder of a sentence and a last sentence, and replacing "Williams" with "Main". A tempting reading is that the underlying park statute being amended may involve cooperative arrangements with outside parties, but nothing in this section's own text establishes or requires consultation, hearings, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision here.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to existing statutory text, specifically correcting punctuation and a proper name. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. There is no interaction with non-federal entities described in this text.

(b) Technical Correction.—Section 1601(c)(8) of Public Law 96–607 (94 Stat. 3547; 16 U.S.C. 41011(c)(8)) is amended by striking “Williams” and inserting “Main”.

opus.w: This section only amends Public Law 96-607: it inserts a period, strikes part of a sentence and a last sentence, and replaces "Williams" with "Main." No outside party (state, local government, public or expert) takes part in any federal decision on the face of the text. Guessing that the struck language involved outside parties is speculation, and in any case deleting text does not require participation.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute could implicitly change participation requirements, but this section is purely a technical correction and amendment of text without introducing any new procedural requirements for outside involvement. It fails against the definition because it does not establish any mechanism for consultation, comment, or coordination with non-federal entities.
